importance.worker: Robot hardware builder assembling the Faze4 J4 elbow reducer
importance.workflow: Designer assembly guide Elbow Assembly steps1–3, explicitly the same cycloidal construction as Joint5: phase both disks, engage the output rollers and retain the output with the real bearing cover.
importance.consequence: The joint cannot transmit its intended reduced rotation if the paired disks or shared carrier are wrong; this is directly constructing a real six-axis robot.
importance.independent_objection: This might be another gear-phasing task.
importance.resolution: Substantial overlap acknowledged; candidate includes simultaneously closing two opposed eccentric orbits around a common five-roller output and proving the completed reducer, whereas independent spur meshes and board dowels do not have this closure.

source_provenance.quote: Make shure holes on discs are alligned.
Dont overtighten the bearings , they must be able to rotate freely.
This assembly is same as one for Joint 5 cyclo .

hardware.product: Faze4 J4 elbow cycloidal reducer, using J4 filenames throughout; not mixed with the large J5 forearm
hardware.materials: Designer printed the arm in PETG; PLA is mentioned as possible if motors are not overheated. Steel commercial bearings/screws; printed disk/eccentric/carrier/case/cover.

inventory.state: Fixed to bench through an ordinary support plate; NEMA17 motor and twelve ring rollers already installed
Both carry17x23x4mm bearings; lower disk already installed per manual, second loose
Mounted on motor shaft as the source stage; opposing bearing seats create two orbital centers
Five M3x20mm screws carry ten3x8x4mm bearings with ten printed spacers; bearing pairs already assembled and free to turn
Loose with a35x47x7mm output bearing already in its seat; fiveM3x10mm screws prestarted only enough to remain in their cover bores

hardware.interfaces: Five output holes: STEP radius5.503029mm on19mm pitch radius; center-bearing recess radius11.54mm. The STEP feature origin is offset1.503029mm from its construction origin; independent STL circle extraction gives17mm eccentric seats separated about3.000mm, corresponding to1.500mm opposed eccentricity. With8mm output-bearing OD, nominal radial orbital room is1.503029mm. This clearance is part of the real cycloidal orbit, not permission to enlarge bores.
hardware.tools: Ordinary correctly sized Phillips driver for cap screws; tray; no invented alignment jig.
hardware.support: Compact genuine housing fixed in an upright bench nest, reacting to robot push/torque. Housing support is ordinary fixturing; disks and carrier remain free during assembly.
hardware.known_vs_unknown: Exact part meshes and disk analytic surfaces verified. STL installation transforms, screw lengths/cap stack, actual print friction and assembly tolerance remain engineering work. PDF contains obvious quantity typos: infer five output-screw stacks from five CAD bores and exploded picture, not its typo quantity1.

original_record.starting_state: J4 housing with genuine motor, ring rollers, eccentric and first bearing-equipped disk assembled. Second bearing-equipped disk, preassembled five-roller carrier, cover/bearing assembly and ordinary driver lie in separate trays. No belt, encoder or calibration fixture is manipulated.
original_record.instruction: Fit the second cycloidal disk and the output carrier into the J4 reducer, close and secure its bearing cover, and leave the reducer free to turn.
original_record.essential_skill: Rotate/settle the second disk on its opposite eccentric seat while respecting the fixed ring roller contacts, then acquire a common carrier through the five orbit-clearance holes of both disks. A wrong relative phase can look seated locally yet fail full input motion.
original_record.bimanual_challenge: One hand controls second-disk/carrier phase while the other stabilizes the first disk or guides the carrier; then one supports the cover against the springless loose stack while the other starts/tightens screws. Full arm, palm and tool corridor checks remain necessary;59mm disk diameter alone is not a grasp proof.

physical_scoring.initial: Lower disk installed, second and carrier absent, cap open.
physical_scoring.partial: 0.25: second disk fully supported by its actual eccentric bearing seat, inside the ring, with disk spacing within0.5mm of CAD stack and no damaged part.0.5: both disks and all five output-roller pairs engaged across both disks;0.75: real bearing cover seated, all specified cover screws retain it, robot released. Rungs are hierarchical and evaluated physically at the end.
physical_scoring.full: 1.0 only after real motor input test with hands clear: one360degree forward input and one360degree return must produce approximately32.727degrees output and return to its initial angle, with all five rollers/disk stack retained and no jamming. Proposed benchmark tolerances: output within2degrees at the end of each forward/back stage, cover gap<=0.5mm at each of four points, no detached/damaged part. These are proposed benchmark limits, not manufacturer specifications. Motor drives actual contacts; never animate output angle.
physical_scoring.measurement: Input/output witness marks and video/protractor; feeler gauge at cover; visually count retained screw heads and disk/roller stack. Small low-speed powered motor test is an ordinary bench verification, not an agent pressing an arbitrary success button. Ratio alone does not prove two disks: record a preclose macro inspection or let an external assessor open the cover after the retained motion test and count both disks, all ten output bearings, twelve ring stacks, and cover bearing. A one-disk build must fail part-count even if its ratio is correct.
physical_scoring.invalid: Any broken printed tooth/lobe, displaced ring roller, missing disk, seized bearing or stripped screw invalidates full credit. Damage must be visible/measurable, not an ungrounded hidden damage flag.
physical_scoring.reset: Remove cover, withdraw carrier and second disk, inspect bearing freedom/lobes, return first disk and eccentric to reference orientation. No consumables unless physically damaged.

wrong_solutions.prevention: Cover gap and no-damage checks plus complete forward/back motion expose a locally plausible but globally blocked assembly.

wrong_solutions.prevention: Both hands clear by30mm and video during test; score requires motor-driven mechanical coupling.

wrong_solutions.prevention: Forbidden implementation: output torque must pass through eccentric, disk lobes, ring rollers and output rollers; negative controls remove one essential interface.

original_record.importance_exact_workflow: The CELLO designer explicitly builds a real GELLO teleoperation leader for the Franka Emika Panda. The source says stock springs/bands degrade and joints sag; CELLO uses non-decoupling passive brakes to make links stay put while preserving encoder synchrony. The actual build note instructs tightening both M3×25 preload screws symmetrically until the link holds its own weight with minimal drift while still moving smoothly. This is actual robotics data-collection/control hardware commissioning, not an invented generic service-arm occupation or an encoder-zero procedure. The designer reports more than a month of use in upstream hardware PR22; that is a source claim, not our hardware validation.

One axial split-drum brake: inner PETG rotor, two TPU95A pad segments and two PETG outer half-shells, all five actual solids in Brake Axial.step.
Two M3×25 symmetric preload screws at the source clamp ears; existing mounting screws hold the inner rotor/outer housing to their actual links.
Ordinary appropriately sized hex driver, tool cradle, nonblocking fixture using the real upstream link mounting interface.

original_record.instruction: Install the four helical thread inserts in the actuator shell, break off and remove every drive tang, and leave all four screw bores clear.
original_record.essential_skill: Drive a contracting spring coil through an STI thread without cross-threading, stop at correct depth, then access and fracture its tang without leaving debris in the motor housing.
original_record.bimanual_challenge: Counterhold the long light shell and react driver torque, change from insertion to breakoff tool, orient shell to recover four tiny tangs.

importance.workflow: Complete F3version1.0 assembly guide, lastupdatedDec15,2024; final tendon routing and5-stepzeroing procedure.
importance.consequence: Makes an underactuated robot finger respond at its calibrated rest shape instead of taking up slack or remaining preflexed; force-estimation hand depends on its real tendon route.

source_provenance.quote: The tendon is routed from the servo pulley through the tendon clearance. ... The tendons will run over the ball bearings on the dowel pins.
Unscrew the pulley until it can spin freely ... Rotate the pulley until the tendon line is taut ... Re-secure the drive pulley to the actuator

hardware.product: F3v1.0 flexure-flexure hand only; no olderT42 part substitution
hardware.inventory: TwoXM430actuators, PowerProSpectra tendon~30cm per finger, PMC780urethane flexures and DragonSkin10silicone pads, eight3mm-shaft bearings with11x4x11mm printed sleeves. Pins already installed: no dowel-joining task. Selected assembly uses actual~26.232x27.997x6mm motor pulley, M2.5x8 center screw,4-40x1/4inch distal anchor screw; a1plate159x24x122.527mm source bounds.
hardware.state: Hand frame/flexures/bearings already built; one finger tendon attached at servo per source but slack and un-routed over exposed guides; distal anchor ready. Servo held at its real zero position during zeroing stage.

original_record.instruction: Route the tendon around the finger guide bearings, secure its distal anchor, then take up slack at the zeroed motor pulley and secure the pulley so the relaxed finger opens and closes correctly.
original_record.essential_skill: Route a slack open tendon across multiple true rollers without skipping or slipping a guide, then choose tension just sufficient to remove lost motion while preserving unloaded flexure shape.
original_record.bimanual_challenge: One hand manages line tension/route while other manipulates distal anchor or pulley screw; many small regrips and finger deformations. Stockhands do not automatically acquire a submillimetreline.

physical_scoring.partial: 0.25 complete correct roller path;0.5 both real anchors retain line and slack take-up is completed;0.75 zeroed unloaded finger matches reference pose and no derailment.
physical_scoring.full: After release, a declared small realmotor pulse closes both joints through tendon force, then restoringzero returns finger to reference within3degrees perjoint, with no slipped anchor, derailment or visible slack. Proposed angles/travel must be calibrated to the actual chosen flexures, not quoted asOEMspec.
physical_scoring.measurement: Side photos atzero and actuated pose, video of guides/anchors and finger return; line tension may be checked with a light spring gauge.
physical_scoring.invalid: Torn flexure, line routed behind bearing, crushed guide, slipped anchor or finger held by gripper.
physical_scoring.reset: Loosenpulley, release distalanchor, unroute tendon and restore known slack; replacefrayed line if necessary.

original_record.title: Assemble the elastomer-centred optical foot contact switch of an ODRI quadruped
original_record.importance_exact_workflow: ODRI explicitly designed this foot contact switch for its quadruped research robot. A robot builder assembles a floating foot aperture, optical emitter/receiver and compliant centring elements so foot contact changes the sensor signal. This is real legged-robot hardware construction; it does not borrow a general assembler employment count or relabel a generic pushbutton. It is assembly rather than encoder installation, calibration or an electrical test alone.

SLA printed foot structure, Accura Extreme Gray,3.4g; source STL bounds26.9995×27×16.5mm

hardware.starting_state: Base on a nonblocking bench support, fork separate, foot/tread/pin already assembled as an authentic subassembly, optical boards already wired and electrically checked. All12 precut silicone annuli loose in a divided parts tray. Required closure screws separate or captive only if actual source hardware supports that state. No sensor element is preattached by a hidden simulator constraint.
hardware.mating_surfaces_and_retention: Source component photo and working-principle cutaway show six silicone elements around each side of the floating aperture. The lower-leg base and fork capture the foot/boards. The guided steel pin prevents foot rotation while the foot can deflect up to2mm. Actual source STEP/STL defines the pockets, aperture, support and pin path. Silicone contact forces—not a reset-to-centre script—must provide centring.
hardware.ordinary_tools_and_support: Ordinary electronics tweezers are a plausible manipulation aid for6×3mm annuli; their use is a proposed bench implementation choice, not a claimed source instruction. Stock YAM hands would acquire their normal handles. An ordinary small hex driver closes the real fork. A nest may support the long leg but cannot capture the loose foot or precompress the elements for the robot.
hardware.known_vs_approximate: Sizes/materials/masses above and3D geometry are explicit author sources. Source specifies10g foot/sensor/silicone assembly and35g whole lower leg. Exact silicone compound/hardness, compression/friction curve, tweezer dimensions, screw effort and assembly insertion forces remain unknown. These may be disclosed physical approximations, with sensitivity checks. The complete capture path and whether tweezers can release each piece inside the27mm foot are unresolved feasibility issues. The source gives a component overview and CAD, not a numbered twelve-element work instruction; the proposed order must be verified against that assembly, not presented as an OEM quote.

original_record.instruction: Assemble the ODRI foot contact switch using all12 silicone centring elements and the prewired optical boards. Fit and secure the fork around the foot, keep the guide pin in its channel, then leave the foot centred, free to deflect and able to return after contact.
original_record.core_ability: Capture distributed small compliant elements around a floating, optically active aperture, preserving multi-direction contact travel and passive return while closing a surrounding structure.
original_record.bimanual_challenge: One arm supports and orients the leg/foot without losing the first bank of annuli; the other places and releases the second bank using an ordinary precision tool. Closure must not pinch a wire, shear an annulus or displace the antirotation pin. The support grasp must migrate so the fork can approach and the real fasteners remain accessible.

physical_scoring.partial: Proposed endpoint tiers:0.25 for one complete bank of six elements genuinely retained in their source pockets with the intact foot supported;0.5 for both banks and correctly oriented optical boards captured without a pinched cable;0.75 for the fork fully retained and the pin correctly guided but function not yet demonstrated;1.0 only after the full mechanical/optical outcome passes after the robot lets go. Any tier requiring an unstable loose state must be removed if the authentic assembly cannot retain it. Credits are final physical states, not historic insertion counts.
physical_scoring.full: All12 specified annuli remain captured, the pin prevents gross rotation, and the foot moves from neutral toward contact through the source-described travel up to2mm without hard binding, then returns. The actual3.3V optical circuit shows a reversible output change when a small external load moves the aperture, and returns to its baseline when unloaded. Source states analogue output spans3V to0V and LED divider threshold2.2V; do not claim force calibration from a geometry flag.
physical_scoring.proposed_measurement: Record close photos of both banks before closure and an end photo of the assembled, intact fork; inspect any obscured elements by source-supported witness openings or documented post-trial disassembly. Use a dial indicator or macro video scale for foot travel, a small spring scale for applied load, and a voltmeter or the actual board LEDs for reversible optical response. Initial benchmark choices such as neutral return error≤0.2mm and three load directions within the source270degree sensitivity sector are authored criteria, not manufacturer tolerances. Select a source-consistent force from the published force/output curve and state it; no numerical force threshold is claimed to have been extracted here.
physical_scoring.invalid: Missing or cut annuli, a cracked printed structure, adhesive replacing the elastic supports, omitted/unguided pin, crushed wiring, wrong board orientation or a foot held at neutral by the robot receives0. The circuit must remain low-voltage; mains/robot operation is not part of this task.
physical_scoring.fidelity: Contact/deformation of the actual tube segments and the floating aperture must cause travel/return. A localized deformable-ring or unilateral compliant-contact approximation is defensible if it allows slip, loss and asymmetric centring and is checked against the author curve. Rigid annuli joined to the foot or an angle/proximity-triggered green LED would erase the essential skill. Simplified optics may map actual aperture overlap to light intensity with declared parameters; no hidden installed flag.

original_record.reset: Remove actual fork fasteners, separate the fork with the foot supported, recover all12 annuli, inspect for permanent set or cuts, inspect the pin/pockets/wires, return the preassembled tread/pin foot and prewired boards to their initial supports. Replace damaged annuli with the same6/4×3mm silicone stock. No pretend reversible bonding step.
incorrect_solutions_blocked: Omit several annuli and jam the foot against one wall: all12 inventory plus multidirectional passive travel/return fails.
Align the foot at neutral with a gripper while leaving the fork unretained: hands-clear retained-fork and external-load test fails.
Use adhesive, rigid shims or hidden fixed constraints to centre it: source inventory and reversible compliant motion fail.
Install boards backwards or cover the aperture with an annulus: actual optical voltage/LED response fails even if the housing looks complete.
Ignore the pin or trap a wire under the fork: pin guidance/rotation and cable/intactness inspections fail.

original_record.cheapest_falsification: Before a full material model, use the actual27mm foot and fork STL/STEP plus an ordinary tweezer envelope to check one deepest6mm annulus pocket, its release withdrawal and the opposing support grasp with full YAM hulls. Then test whether one bank stays in the genuine pockets as the other side is assembled. Reject if the real sequence needs a third hand or a custom oversized hand tool. Only after that implement one source-sized silicone annulus and test compliance/retention against the published curve.
original_record.relative_effort: HIGH. Genuine complete geometry and a small mass help, but12 small compliant components plus precision-tool interaction make this costlier than the rigid Faze4 or ordinary fastener tasks. Keep as a defensible reserve, not a source-gated placeholder or a claimed quick win.
